newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Investors to press Jardine Fleming for redress.
newsitem.headline: Investors to press Jardine Fleming for redress.

text.p: Some investors are pressing for compensation for losses incurred from a fund managed by Colin Armstrong, a disgraced former fund manager with a unit of Jardine Fleming Holdings Ltd, a newspaper said on Friday.

The South China Morning Post reported that Bill Glover, a retired managing director and chairman of Matheson PFC, the personal financial planning arm of Jardine Matheson, would convene a group to seek redress.

Regulators in London and Hong Kong uncovered in August a series of irregular trades by the former senior fund manager in Hong Kong at the firm's fund management subsidiary, Jardine Fleming Investment Management, after a five-month probe.
The firm was fined 700,000 sterling and had authorisation of its London-based fund company withdrawn.

The newspaper quoted Glover as saying that some 50 investors offered to support him after he announced his intention to seek redress from Jardine Fleming for alleged personal losses of about US$68,000 from his investment in the Jardine Fleming Pacific Securities Trust, previously managed by Armstrong.
Glover was quoted as saying the group intended to raise enough funds to seek a legal opinion from a Queen's Counsel about the compensation claim.
Neither Glover nor Jardine Fleming was immediately available for comment.
